title: Volume: a sane starting level, and controls

units.title: Measure our loudness against mGBA and real apps
units.detail: Answers what 'correct' volume is. Today runtime::sound::mix maps the 10-bit DAC's full swing to full i16 (x64), and desktop audio.rs plays it at /32768 with no gain, so a game that swings the DAC fully plays at 0 dBFS. Measure peak and loudness (RMS or LUFS; Rust, not a python script) of our --wav against mgba-dump --audio-log for the same frames on 3+ ROMs (agb sound ROM, Emerald title/overworld/battle, Kirby AM): the dB gap to mGBA at its default 100%, and how loud each is next to typical desktop audio (~-14 to -23 LUFS). Write the numbers and a recommended default gain into docs/sound-design.md 'Playback'. Leave mix() alone: the oracle and audio hashes depend on it.

record.evidence: just audio-loudness on 8 scenes, 7 ROMs (agb sound ROM, 10512 Hz ROM, Emerald intro/title/Littleroot, Kirby AM, Minish Cap, Metroid ZM): ours is +2.50 dB RMS over mGBA at 100% in every one (x64 vs mGBA's x48), -6.5 to -19.3 LUFS. Table and recommended -6 dB default gain in docs/sound-design.md 'Level'; loudness tool unit-tested against BS.1770 (0 LUFS 997 Hz sine); just check passes after merging main.

units.title: Start at a reasonable volume by default
units.detail: Apply a master gain in the desktop (f32, before the resampler in audio.rs; never in runtime mix(), which the audio hashes and mGBA oracle judge), defaulting to the level {unit:volume/measure-level} recommends. Headless --wav/--audio-hash stay ungained. Netplay's seat sound gets the same gain. Evidence: before/after peak and loudness on the same ROMs.

record.evidence: Player applies DEFAULT_GAIN x0.5 (f32, before the resampler) for window, link and netplay seats; mix()/--wav/--audio-hash ungained. Ungained --wav vs new --audio-pace 0 --played-wav, same frames: agb -14.4->-20.5 LUFS, Emerald -15.4->-21.9, Kirby -19.3->-25.9, Minish -12.5->-19.0, Metroid -6.5->-12.8; peaks -6.02..-6.05 dB. Test the_gain_scales_what_plays; just check passes. Table in docs/sound-design.md Level.

notes.text: Measured in {unit:volume/measure-level}: ours is 2.50 dB over mGBA at 100%; -6.5 to -19 LUFS. Recommended -6 dB (x0.5) in playback after the resampler; -2.5 dB would match mGBA. Table: docs/sound-design.md 'Level'; rerun with just audio-loudness.

units.title: Find why sound starts very loud on Windows
units.detail: A friend reported the Windows build started very loud (louder than Linux, which is also loud). Suspects: WASAPI shared mode has no per-app default below 100% where PipeWire may restore a lower stream volume; the device's sample format (cpal I16/U16/I32 paths in audio/device.rs) or channel count (5.1/7.1 interleave) scaling wrong; Windows loudness enhancements. Check what can be checked by reading cpal and our conversion, and in wine if it helps. Real-Windows confirmation goes on {unit:stretch/windows-play-gate} as a note, not here. Agents may not touch june's screen for Windows (decision).

record.evidence: Read cpal 0.18.2 WASAPI (shared mode, GetMixFormat F32, AUTOCONVERTPCM, session volume never set: 100% of master), dasp f32->int conv (correct, saturating) and our interleave (L/R then silence, right for 5.1/7.1). No format/channel bug; the report predates the -6 dB default; host differences (PipeWire restored stream volume, Windows Loudness Equalization). Written in docs/sound-design.md Level; just check passes.

Flag --volume PCT (0-200, 100=DEFAULT_GAIN -6 dB, 200 ungained) or 'volume = PCT' in settings.conf sets the gain for window, link and netplay seats and --audio-pace's --played-wav. New settings.rs parses/loads both keys; set/save rewrite one in place (for the menu row). Tests the_settings_file, the_volume_flag. agb sound ROM 600 frames played-wav peaks: -19.32 dBFS at 100, -25.34 at 50, -13.30 at 200 (6.02 dB steps). just check passes.

units.title: Volume and mute rows in the window menu
units.detail: In menu.rs's main page: a Volume row (left/right in 10% steps, like Fast-forward's) and a Mute toggle that pauses output without stopping the device's pacing (see how fast-forward empties the queue). Changes save to settings.conf. Works by pad and keyboard. Test the row logic in Rust; a screenshot in a cu session for evidence.

record.evidence: Volume (10% steps, 0-200, saved to settings.conf, comments kept) and Mute (gain 0 + queue emptied, device keeps pacing) rows; tests volumes_step_and_stop_at_the_ends, the_volume_and_mute_rows_set_and_save_it, muting_keeps_the_device_pacing; just check 722 pass after merging main. cu session (keyboard; cu has no headless pad): screenshot work/volume-menu-row/menu-volume-mute.png shows Volume 120%, Mute on; settings.conf rewritten to 'volume = 120 # starting level'; muted run 0 underruns, presents mean 16.6 ms.

notes.text: Use settings::save(path, "volume", pct) to persist (rewrites the line, comments kept); Player::set_gain(audio::volume_gain(pct)) to apply live. Volume is 0-200 percent, 100 = default -6 dB level.

units.title: Volume keys with a brief on-screen level
units.detail: Keyboard keys to step volume and mute without opening the menu (pick ones that don't clash with remap defaults, e.g. - = and M or F-keys), saved like the menu's. Show the level for ~1 s on screen (egui toast or runtime overlay.rs). No pad combo unless one is free of game buttons.

record.evidence: With the menu shut, - and = (keypad - +) step the volume 10% (saved to settings.conf like the menu's row, unmuting) and M mutes for the run; an egui toast shows 'Volume N%' or 'Muted' for 1 s. Keys are free in the default and player-2 maps (test the_volume_keys_are_free); a key a mapping binds stays the button's. Menu test the_volume_keys_step_mute_save_and_toast; just check passes after merging main. No pad combo: none free.
